subject: Close ramp & GPU pool sizing decisions for MAP
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Park <apark@novumlabs.com>, Natasha Kumar <natasha.k@novumlabs.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Close ramp & GPU pool sizing decisions for MAP

Alex / Natasha —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion Ilya and your infra team want clarity on three items to lock the MAP and the reservation:

- Target steady-state QPS and peak ramp multiplier (you mentioned 4x for demo spikes)
- Maximum acceptable cold-start latency (p50/p95 targets) to size the staging pool vs production pool
- Preferred tranche cadence (single commit vs two tranches across 90 days)

I attached a draft mutual action plan with two sizing options and a blank GPU sizing sheet for your team to populate. Can you confirm the steady-state token throughput and the desired SLA band by EOD Tuesday so we can finalize the dedicated pool proposal and the procurement window?

Attachments: novum_map_draft_v3.pdf (MAP draft), gpu-sizing-sheets.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

From: Alex Park <apark@novumlabs.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Natasha Kumar <natasha.k@novumlabs.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 11:03:12 -0000
Subject: Re: Close ramp & GPU pool sizing decisions for MAP

Irene —

Appreciate the crisp agenda and the draft. Quick answers from our side:

- Steady-state: ~60 requests/min with average 800 tokens/request (roughly 48k tokens/min). Peak multiplier: 3.5x for launch week; planning headroom to 5x for marketing-driven spikes.
- Latency target: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 450ms — anything above p95 600ms degrades UX for the live demo.
- Tranche preference: we'd prefer a two-tranche approach (40% initial, 60% post-acceptance) to align with budget cycles, but open to a single commit if it reduces lead time.

I'll take a pass at the gpu-sizing sheet and return it with our notes by Monday. Also looping in our procurement lead, Natasha.

Thanks,
Alex Park
Head of Platform Engineering | Novum Labs
apark@novumlabs.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 8 Aug 2026 14:30:10 -0000
Subject: RE: Close ramp & GPU pool sizing decisions for MAP

Team —

I pulled together a quick sizing matrix based on Novum's numbers (60 req/min, 800 tokens/req, 3.5x peak, 5x headroom). Key calls / tradeoffs:

- Option A (Minimal on-prem/dedicated): 6x A100 80GB instances in the prod pool, 2x for staging. This meets p50/p95 with small batching and gives a fast procurement window if we use pre-negotiated OEM SKU bundles.
- Option B (Latency-prioritized): 8x A100 80GB + 2x 8-bit quantized replicas for cost-optimized bursts (NVMe-backed local cache). This lowers p95 in tests by ~20% but increases procurement lead time by 3–4 weeks.
- Buffer plan: reserve an extra 20% burst buffer via Dedicated burst capacity for the first 30 days to cover marketing spikes while Novum confirms traffic patterns.

Attachments: gpu-sizing-sheets_filled-Novum.xlsx (I converted Alex's estimates into per-model token/sec and latency sims).

Ask: Marissa / Karthik — can you confirm which procurement path shortens lead time the most (marketplace vs OEM PO) and whether finance can accept a two-tranche contract with an initial 40% commit? I will note SOC2 checklist items that may impact onboarding lead time.

Rishi
Head of Capacity Planning | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Park <apark@novumlabs.com>, Natasha Kumar <natasha.k@novumlabs.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 16:45:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Close ramp & GPU pool sizing decisions for MAP

Alex / Natasha —

Thanks for the fast turnaround, everyone. Summary and next steps so we can formalize the MAP and hit procurement windows: 

1) MAP & sizing selected: we recommend Option B (latency-prioritized) with the burst buffer enabled for launch week. This aligns with your p95 goal and demo needs.
2) Procurement cadence: two tranches (40% up-front, 60% after acceptance) — finance indicated this is acceptable pending a standard P.O. and DocuSign SOW.
3) Lead times: OEM procurement path adds ~4 weeks; marketplace listing (reserved Dedicated bundles) can reduce lead time to ~10 business days but requires acceptance of pre-configured SKUs. We will include a clause allowing temporary Dedicated burst capacity while OEM order completes.
4) SOC2/onboarding: Irene will provide the SOC2 answer matrix and evidence bucket (Irene: attach SOC2 timeline zip).

Asks for Novum: please sign the attached MAP draft (DocuSign link) and confirm the filled gpu-sizing sheet by Thursday COB so procurement can start the marketplace reservation. We will provision burst capacity the day the PO is issued.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/eq/DEAL-7345
Attachments referenced: novum_map_draft_v3.pdf, gpu-sizing-sheets.xlsx, soc2_timeline.zip

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0199
